question: Which economic reform allowed multinational corporations to enter the Indian market?
solution: The correct answer is __**Globalisation**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Globalisation** refers to the process of increasing economic, political, cultural, and technological interdependence between countries, leading to the integration of world markets. • In the **Indian context**, globalisation began with the **Liberalisation Policy of 1991**, initiated under the leadership of then Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**. • The **economic reforms of 1991** included policies such as the removal of trade barriers, deregulation of industries, and the opening up of the economy to foreign investments, allowing **multinational corporations (MNCs)** to enter the Indian market. • Globalisation enabled Indian industries to compete globally, fostered foreign investments, and encouraged technological advancements and cultural exchanges. • As a result, sectors such as **IT, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and manufacturing** witnessed rapid growth due to the entry of MNCs and the availability of international markets.
